paper_title: Aerobic Oxidation of Propargylic Alcohols to α,β-Unsaturated Alkynals or Alkynones Catalyzed by Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, TEMPO and Sodium Chloride in Toluene

questions.question: In the paper, what does the abbreviation 'DCE' refer to?
What is the name of product 2b as given in the paper (structure/identified name)?
What solvent, catalyst loading (Fe and TEMPO), atmosphere, temperature and reaction time were used for the room-temperature oxidation of substrate 1a to ketone 2a in Table 1?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Solvent: toluene; catalysts/additives: Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (5 mol%), TEMPO (3 mol%), NaCl (5 mol%); atmosphere: O2; temperature: room temperature (r.t.); time: 2 h

questions.question: For substrate 1b (R = H) converted to 2b, which method reported in Table 2 (Method A or Method B) gave the higher isolated yield, and what were the two isolated yields?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Method B gave the higher isolated yield: Method A = 77% (2b), Method B = 91% (2b)
